task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 idiom gate (WF-02 Step 2d equivalent) on the ISS-0106 fix. Review `git diff main...HEAD`. SECURITY-REVIEWER passed it at Step 3c ahead of you.

NOTE ON YOUR PRIOR TURN IN THIS RUN: you also wrote the decision-record amendment at Step 1.5 that this implementation carries out. That does NOT make this step self-review of your own producer work -- the amendment decided WHAT to do and this gate checks HOW it was built, by CODE-DESIGNER and ELIXIR-DEV. But it does mean you are unusually well placed to catch the one thing nobody else can: whether the implementation actually honours the decision, or quietly drifted from it while appearing to comply. Check that specifically.

WHAT IS IN THE DIFF: (A) .tool-versions repinned to Elixir 1.20.3 / OTP 29 (erlang 29.0.5), a NEW mix task lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex, the letflow.check alias gaining that task as its first step, and README/developer-guide text; (B) four files reformatted; (C) sixteen struct-update bind-site annotations in lib/letflow/engine/{transition,reconstruction,sub_process}.ex and lib/letflow/engine.ex.

FIVE THINGS TO GATE ON, beyond your normal idiom/supervision/scope-creep checks:

  1. **DECISION-RECORD FIDELITY.** Your own amendment (the section dated 2026-08-21T01:25:50Z at the end of docs/migration/decisions/0005-pin-formatting-toolchain.md) stated the decision so it could be implemented without inference. Check each of its numbered points against what actually shipped -- especially point 2, that mix.exs's `elixir: "~> 1.18"` is UNCHANGED. ELIXIR-DEV reports the mix.exs diff hunk begins at line 53 and so cannot have touched line 8; verify that yourself rather than accepting it, because a change there would silently lock the only confirmed-live host out of compiling.

  2. **THE THREE PROPERTIES THE OPTION WAS CONDITIONAL ON.** Your amendment adopted the version check only as an unsuppressible warning that never alters another check's exit code. Verify in the shipped code, not in the design doc: no raising construct on any path (including `throw`, which the design's own verification list originally omitted), no environment variable or switch read, output on stderr rather than through `Mix.shell()`, and the outer guard carrying BOTH a `rescue` and a `catch` clause. ELIXIR-DEV reports proving non-suppressibility empirically by piping stdout away; you may re-run that or verify structurally, but say which you did.

  3. **THE COUNT CHANGED FROM 14 TO 16 AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART.** Three prior steps independently measured 14 sites; fixing them unmasked two more of the same class, because the compiler could not see past the first inference failure per function. Confirm the two additional sites are genuinely the same class and the same idiom, and not something else that got swept in under cover of a count that was expected to move. Confirm also that zero warnings were reached by fixing rather than silencing -- no `@compile`, `nowarn`, `@dialyzer`, or warnings-as-errors escape anywhere in the diff. That is core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures' applied to the exact gate this run exists to turn green, which makes it the most tempting place in the whole run to cheat.

  4. **AN IDIOM-CONSISTENCY OBSERVATION HANDED TO YOU BY SECURITY-REVIEWER**, explicitly as an idiom call rather than a security one: `dispatch_parallel_gateway/4` (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:605) annotates both `instance_state` and `token`, while the function it delegates to, `dispatch_parallel_split/4` (transition.ex:656), annotates only `instance_state`. Rule on it. Either verdict is fine -- but if you require a change, it must be a real improvement rather than a symmetry preference, and note that adding an annotation where the compiler did not ask for one is a behaviour change (a struct pattern raises where a bare variable binds), so a request here is not cost-free.

  5. **SCOPE CREEP, in both directions.** The decision's scope was Parts A/B/C and nothing else. Check nothing extra rode along -- and equally, that nothing mandated was quietly dropped, including the two documentation items (README's measurably-false 'accepts any 1.18.x patch' claim, and docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md line 17's stale 'Elixir 1.17+ / OTP 26+'), which are easy to skip because they are prose rather than code.

DO NOT gate on the currently-failing test suite. `mix letflow.check` exits 1 at its `letflow.check.test` step; ELIXIR-DEV and SECURITY-REVIEWER independently observed 13-14 failures confined to Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest and Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest, none touching the four engine modules, and ELIXIR-DEV attributed them as pre-existing by stashing its changes back to HEAD and re-running against the same database. Attribution is TEST-RUNNER's job at Step 4. It concerns you only if you find reason to believe a failure is caused by this diff.
acceptance_criteria: Every numbered point of the 2026-08-21T01:25:50Z decision amendment is checked against what shipped, with a per-point verdict -- including the mix.exs line-8 no-op, verified by your own inspection rather than by accepting the reported diff-hunk line number

The three conditional properties (no raising path including throw; no env-var or switch read; stderr not Mix.shell(); guard with both rescue and catch) are each verified against the SHIPPED code with the method stated
The two additional Part C sites (14 -> 16) are confirmed to be the same warning class and the same idiom, by your own inspection
The diff is confirmed to contain no warning-suppression mechanism of any kind (@compile, nowarn, @dialyzer, warnings-as-errors escapes, or equivalent), with the check you ran quoted

A ruling is given on the dispatch_parallel_gateway/dispatch_parallel_split annotation asymmetry, with reasoning, and if a change is required the reason it is an improvement rather than a symmetry preference
Scope checked in both directions: nothing beyond Parts A/B/C rode along, and nothing mandated was dropped -- explicitly including the two documentation items

Ordinary idiom review performed on the new mix task: OTP/Elixir idiom, error handling shape, module and function naming against this repo's conventions, and whether the moduledoc states the mechanisms it is required to state
PASS or FAIL stated, with any FAIL naming each specific gap and what would close it
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
PASS. Nine acceptance criteria checked; no gap found; no rework requested. Everything below was re-derived from the shipped tree, not read out of the design doc or the implementation handoff.

(1) DECISION-RECORD FIDELITY -- all seven numbered scope points of the 2026-08-21T01:25:50Z amendment honoured. Point 1: `.tool-versions` is exactly `elixir 1.20.3-otp-29` / `erlang 29.0.5`. Point 2 (the one I was told not to take on report): VERIFIED BY MY OWN INSPECTION, not by accepting the reported hunk line. I diffed the file's head on both sides -- `git show main:mix.exs | sed -n 1,20p` and `git show HEAD:mix.exs | sed -n 1,20p` -- and line 8 reads `elixir: "~> 1.18"` identically in both. Corroborated independently with `git diff main...HEAD -U0 -- mix.exs | grep '^@@'`, which reports exactly two hunks, `@@ -55,0 +56,8 @@` and `@@ -56,0 +65 @@`; both are pure insertions in the aliases block and neither has a deletion range, so nothing anywhere in the file was replaced. The only confirmed-live host stays able to compile. Point 3: `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex` exists and does what the point specifies. Point 4: `"letflow.check_toolchain"` is the literal first element of the `letflow.check` alias list, ahead of `format --check-formatted`. Point 5: README's Notes carry the new pin AND the measurably-false 'accepts any 1.18.x patch' sentence is gone, replaced by the measured `>= 1.18.0 and < 2.0.0` semantics plus the reason the requirement is deliberately wider than the pin, plus a standing note that narrowing it needs REVIEWER sign-off. Point 6: `docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md:17` no longer says 'Elixir 1.17+ / OTP 26+ (scaffolded on 1.14/OTP 25 via apt)'; it names the pin, says the version is load-bearing, and states the warned-not-blocked rule. Point 7: the record itself needed no further edit and got none.

(2) THE THREE CONDITIONAL PROPERTIES -- verified STRUCTURALLY AND EMPIRICALLY; stating which for each. Structural, by grep over the shipped file (`grep -nE 'raise|throw|exit\(|Mix\.raise|System\.halt|System\.stop|[a-z_]+!\(|Mix\.shell|System\.get_env|OptionParser|System\.argv' lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex` -> exit 1, ZERO matches): no raising construct on any path including `throw`; no `Mix.raise`, `System.halt`, `System.stop`, or any `!`-suffixed call -- the code uses `File.cwd/0` and `File.read/1`, never the bang forms; no environment-variable read and no switch parsing at all (`run/1` takes `_args` and ignores it, so non-suppressibility is an absence of mechanism rather than a promise); all warning output goes through `warn_block/2`, whose only emitter is `IO.puts(:stderr, &1)` -- `Mix.shell()` appears nowhere. The outer guard at `run/1` carries BOTH clauses: `rescue error ->` and `catch kind, value ->`, each routing to `internal_error/1`, which itself does no version lookup so it cannot fail in turn. Every terminal function returns `:ok` (`warn_block/2` ends in `Enum.each/2`).

Empirically, I did not merely re-run ELIXIR-DEV's probe in-tree -- on this host the toolchain matches the pin, so the in-tree run proves nothing about the drift path. I ran the drift path out of tree instead, from a scratch directory containing a fabricated `elixir 1.18.3-otp-27` / `erlang 27.2` pin file, loading the compiled beam with `-pa`, under `MIX_QUIET=1`, with `--quiet --silent --no-warn` passed as arguments and stdout redirected to /dev/null. The full TOOLCHAIN OFF PIN block still appeared (both rows, both `<-- MISMATCH`), `run/1` returned `:ok`, and the exit code was 0. A second scratch directory with no pin file at all produced the TOOLCHAIN PIN NOT CHECKED block, also exit 0 -- so graceful degradation is measured, not asserted. Repo state was untouched by both probes.

One non-blocking observation, recorded rather than requested: the MATCH path (`report/3`, line 304) prints its 'OK' line with a bare `IO.puts/1`, i.e. to stdout, while every warning path goes to stderr. This is the correct way round -- the stream that must survive a stdout pipe is the warning, and it does -- so there is nothing to fix. Noting it only so a later reader does not mistake the asymmetry for an oversight and 'correct' it by moving the warning onto stdout.

(3) 14 -> 16, THE MOST TEMPTING PLACE IN THE RUN TO CHEAT. I reconstructed the count from the diff myself rather than accepting it. Sixteen annotations ship: transition.ex 7, reconstruction.ex 7, sub_process.ex 1, engine.ex 1. Against the design's C1-C14 table the two additions are precisely identifiable: (i) `dispatch_parallel_gateway/4`'s `instance_state`, in transition.ex, and (ii) the `apply_event/4` `"SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED"` clause's `state`, in reconstruction.ex. Both are the same warning class (`struct for X is expected on struct update`), the same struct (`InstanceState`), and the same idiom (an explicit struct pattern at the bind site, ISS-0046's already-merged remedy) -- no other kind of change rode in under cover of a moving count. The unmasking story checks out at the source level, which is the part worth verifying: each addition sits in the SAME FUNCTION as an already-listed site, which is exactly where a one-inference-failure-per-function compiler would hide a second one. In `dispatch_parallel_gateway/4` the listed site C4 was the `Token` update `%Token{token | node_id: edge.target}`; the newly-visible one is the `InstanceState` update on the very next line, `%InstanceState{instance_state | tokens: new_tokens}`. In the `"SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED"` clause the listed site C11 was `parked_token`, updated at `%Token{parked_token | waiting_child_instance_id: ...}`; the newly-visible one is `state`, updated a few lines below at `%InstanceState{state | variables: ..., tokens: ...}`. Two functions, two second-failures, two additions -- the arithmetic and the mechanism agree.

Zero warnings were reached by FIXING, not by silencing. `git diff main...HEAD` over the non-doc, non-handoff paths, grepped for `@compile|nowarn|@dialyzer|warnings_as_errors|warnings-as-errors|--no-warn|@moduledoc false` on added lines, returns exactly ONE hit, and it is prose: mix.exs line 685 of the diff, the words 'compile --warnings-as-errors' inside an explanatory comment. No attribute, no flag, no `elixirc_options`, no escape of any kind. The gate itself is not weakened: mix.exs's only functional change is the single prepended alias entry. Positive confirmation rather than absence-of-evidence: I ran `MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`, a full 90-file rebuild from scratch so nothing could hide in a stale manifest -- 'Compiling 90 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app', no warning text, exit 0. And `mix format --check-formatted` exits 0, so Symptom 1 is genuinely closed rather than tolerated.

(4) RULING ON THE dispatch_parallel_gateway / dispatch_parallel_split ASYMMETRY (SECURITY-REVIEWER's idiom hand-off): NO CHANGE REQUIRED. The asymmetry is correct and should stay. It is not an inconsistency -- it is the compiler's demand recorded faithfully in both places. `dispatch_parallel_gateway/4` performs a struct update on `token` (`%Token{token | node_id: edge.target}`, the `:pass_through` branch), so the annotation there was compiler-demanded; it appears in the design's own table as C4, sourced from the compiler's 'when defining the variable' remedy line. `dispatch_parallel_split/4` never updates `token` -- it only reads `token.token_id` and builds fresh `%Token{}` literals -- so the compiler never asked, and nothing was suppressed by leaving it bare. Adding one for symmetry would be a pure aesthetic edit with a real cost, exactly as flagged: a struct pattern raises where a bare variable binds, so it would introduce a new runtime failure mode at a site where no type question exists, and it would blur the property that makes this diff auditable -- that every annotation present traces to a specific compiler diagnostic. The rule the diff follows, and should keep following, is 'annotate where the compiler asked, nowhere else.' Both functions obey it.

(5) SCOPE, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Nothing extra rode along: `git diff main...HEAD --name-status` lists 23 paths, and every one maps to Part A (`.tool-versions`, mix.exs, the new task, README, backend_developer_guide), Part B (pin_resolver.ex, variable_merge.ex, pin_rebind_test.exs, pin_resolver_test.exs), Part C (transition.ex, reconstruction.ex, sub_process.ex, engine.ex), or the run's own paper trail (decision record, design doc, eight handoffs). No new dependency, no config change, no migration, no unrelated refactor. Part B is mechanical and I checked it line by line for a semantic change smuggled into a reformat: three line-wraps at 99-102 chars, and one heredoc `"""` -> `\"""` escape inside variable_merge.ex's moduledoc that renders identically. Nothing mandated was dropped, including both prose items, which are the easy ones to skip -- README's false claim is deleted (verified by reading the new text, not by trusting the file appearing in the diffstat) and backend_developer_guide.md:17 is rewritten. Absent by design and correctly so: there is no test file for the new task, because tests are TEST-DESIGNER's at Step 4; adding them here would itself have been scope creep.

ORDINARY IDIOM REVIEW OF THE NEW TASK. Module and file naming match the repo's existing convention exactly (`Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchain` in `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex`, alongside the existing `letflow.check.test.ex`). `use Mix.Task`, `@shortdoc`, `@impl Mix.Task`, and a `@spec run([String.t()]) :: :ok` are all present and correct. Error handling is idiomatic Elixir rather than defensive Elixir: the parse is total by construction, so there is no parse-failure branch to get wrong; failure modes F1-F8 are each a named `case` clause on a tagged tuple, not a rescue; the `try` is a deliberate outer backstop for the never-fails guarantee rather than control flow. Private helpers are small, single-purpose, and all `@spec`'d. The moduledoc states every mechanism it is required to state -- that the task is advisory and returns `:ok` on all paths, why ordering lives in the alias data rather than in the module, why stderr rather than `Mix.shell()`, why there is no suppression surface, and the OTP major-vs-full-version asymmetry together with the false-positive it exists to prevent. Two forward-looking prohibitions are written into the doc where the next reader will hit them ('a later change must not add [a suppression surface]' and 'a later run must not "fix" this by tightening the comparison'), which is the right place for them.

No supervision or `:gen_statem` surface is touched anywhere in this diff -- no process, supervisor, or state-machine callback is added, removed, or moved -- so per-instance isolation via `Letflow.InstanceSupervisor` is untouched. On type-safety: Part C is itself the strengthening move, converting sixteen implicit type assumptions into explicit struct patterns at their bind sites; I found no additional unrepresentable-invalid-state gap worth filing under `docs/issues/`.

I did NOT gate on the failing suite, as instructed. I did check the narrower question that is mine: whether anything in this diff could cause a failure. A forced full rebuild is clean and the format gate is green, and the four engine modules are touched only by struct patterns whose types the surrounding `@spec`s already asserted. I found no reason to believe this diff causes any of the reported failures. Attribution remains TEST-RUNNER's at Step 4.

Process note: no file outside `handoffs/` was modified by this step (`git status --porcelain` shows only this handoff plus ORCH's own `registry.json`, `orchestrator.log`, and untracked `docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml`, all left alone). Both empirical probes ran in the scratch directory. No `docker compose up` was run.
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGNER (WF-03 Step 4). The idiom gate is green, so test design is unblocked. Two things worth carrying into that step: (1) `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex` ships with no tests, deliberately -- its eight named failure modes F1-F8, the OTP major-vs-full asymmetry, and above all the never-fails-the-build property are the coverage targets, and the out-of-tree probe technique recorded in this handoff's summary (scratch cwd + fabricated .tool-versions + `-pa` against the compiled beam) is a working way to exercise the drift path without touching the repo's own pin file. (2) Attribution of the currently-failing suite is TEST-RUNNER's, not TEST-DESIGNER's; this gate found no reason to believe the diff causes any of it.
